questions.q: How does the editorial describe spirituality?
options: As a gift given only to mystics
Not quite. The article says: As a conscious discovery by the thinking mind of a reality beyond the material.
As a passing mood of ecstasy
Not quite. The article says: As a conscious discovery by the thinking mind of a reality beyond the material.
As a conscious discovery by the thinking mind of a reality beyond the material
Yes. It is called the highest intellectual achievement.
As the suppression of all thought
Not quite. The article says: As a conscious discovery by the thinking mind of a reality beyond the material.
questions.rationale: “Spirituality is a phenomenon of intellectual development. By applying the mind, one discovers that there is a non-material reality beyond material existence.”

questions.article: The Role of Muslims in Diaspora
questions.q: The first Muslims who migrated to Abyssinia are held up as a model. How did they live there?
options: As guests supported by the king
Not quite. The article says: In harmony with local people, earning their living by hard work and ready to help defend the country.
As traders who soon returned home
Not quite. The article says: In harmony with local people, earning their living by hard work and ready to help defend the country.
Apart from the local people, by their own laws
Not quite. The article says: In harmony with local people, earning their living by hard work and ready to help defend the country.
In harmony with local people, earning their living by hard work and ready to help defend the country
Right. As givers, not takers.
questions.rationale: “The Muslims who went to live in Abyssinia created no problems for the local people. They lived in harmony with others and earned their livelihood through hard labor.”

questions.article: The Role of Muslims in Diaspora
questions.q: Which verse does the article quote to show that an oath of citizenship must be honoured?
options: “There is no compulsion in religion”
Not quite. The article says: “Keep your promises; you will be called to account for every promise which you have made”.
“Keep your promises; you will be called to account for every promise which you have made”
“For you your religion; for me mine”
Not quite. The article says: “Keep your promises; you will be called to account for every promise which you have made”.
“Reconciliation is best”
Not quite. The article says: “Keep your promises; you will be called to account for every promise which you have made”.
questions.rationale: “The word ‘promises’ here includes all kinds of promises, big or small… if a Muslim takes an oath of allegiance to a foreign country, it is incumbent on him to abide by it.”

questions.article: Keeping Calm in the Face of Adversity
questions.q: Facing 20,000 soldiers with a handful of men, Napoleon walked forward unarmed and won them over. What does the article take from this?
options: One who stays calm in danger can judge the situation and find a way other than confrontation
Well read. Panic prevents a proper assessment.
Armies are loyal only to the strong
Not quite. The article says: One who stays calm in danger can judge the situation and find a way other than confrontation.
Courage always defeats numbers
Not quite. The article says: One who stays calm in danger can judge the situation and find a way other than confrontation.
Battles are won by speeches
Not quite. The article says: One who stays calm in danger can judge the situation and find a way other than confrontation.
questions.rationale: “Whatever a man’s resources, to deal effectively with a situation, he must be able to make a proper assessment. And he will not be able to do this if he panics in the face of danger.”

questions.q: How does the article distinguish a negative person from a positive one?
options: One is silent; the other speaks out
Not quite. The article says: One is a victim of circumstances and laments them; the other rises above them and helps shape history.
One is poor; the other rich
Not quite. The article says: One is a victim of circumstances and laments them; the other rises above them and helps shape history.
One is young; the other experienced
Not quite. The article says: One is a victim of circumstances and laments them; the other rises above them and helps shape history.
One is a victim of circumstances and laments them; the other rises above them and helps shape history
Correct. Negative thinking rests on the outer world, positive thinking on one’s inner self.
questions.rationale: “A negative person is a victim of history, while a positive person helps shape history.”

questions.q: Paul Dirac was an unremarkable engineering student who became one of the great physicists. What does the article conclude?
options: Engineering is harder than mathematics
Not quite. The article says: Everyone has a field of his own in which to excel; failure in one is no reason to lose hope.
Teachers cannot recognise genius
Not quite. The article says: Everyone has a field of his own in which to excel; failure in one is no reason to lose hope.
Everyone has a field of his own in which to excel; failure in one is no reason to lose hope
Yes. Mathematics was his “home ground.”
Success depends on the right college
Not quite. The article says: Everyone has a field of his own in which to excel; failure in one is no reason to lose hope.

questions.article: The Universe Is Not a Machine
questions.q: The article tells of robots that went out of control. What argument does it build on such accidents?
options: Technology should be abandoned
Not quite. The article says: A mere machine goes wrong; the faultless order of the universe over billions of years points to conscious control.
The universe is a larger robot
Not quite. The article says: A mere machine goes wrong; the faultless order of the universe over billions of years points to conscious control.
Machines will one day replace people
Not quite. The article says: A mere machine goes wrong; the faultless order of the universe over billions of years points to conscious control.
A mere machine goes wrong; the faultless order of the universe over billions of years points to conscious control
Well reasoned. “Each in its own orbit runs.”
questions.rationale: “Had the universe just been a mechanical object like the robot, there would definitely have been accidents similar to those mentioned above.”

questions.q: “Fake notes can be passed on the streets, but banks will not accept them.” What does this comparison explain?
options: Banks are more honest than markets
Not quite. The article says: Pretence may pass in this world, but not in the next, where only what is truly in the heart will count.
Pretence may pass in this world, but not in the next, where only what is truly in the heart will count
Yes. Words will no longer bear false meanings.
The poor will be rich in the next world
Not quite. The article says: Pretence may pass in this world, but not in the next, where only what is truly in the heart will count.
Money has no value after death
Not quite. The article says: Pretence may pass in this world, but not in the next, where only what is truly in the heart will count.
questions.rationale: “In the next world it will not be possible to make lies appear true, and injustice appear like justice.”

options: The worship of money
Right. It sees this among the outwardly religious too.
The worship of science
Not quite. The article says: The worship of money.
The worship of ancestors
Not quite. The article says: The worship of money.
The worship of nature
Not quite. The article says: The worship of money.

options: A sudden death is a misfortune
Not quite. The article says: Death comes to everyone at an appointed moment; wise is the one who prepares before it.
Death comes to everyone at an appointed moment; wise is the one who prepares before it
Yes. “Successful is the one who awakens” in time.
Lecturing is dangerous in old age
Not quite. The article says: Death comes to everyone at an appointed moment; wise is the one who prepares before it.
Public men should retire early
Not quite. The article says: Death comes to everyone at an appointed moment; wise is the one who prepares before it.
questions.rationale: “Death comes to everyone… a point of no return… Wise is the one who tries to prepare himself for this moment.”
